assumptions: Took the issue's recommended fix shape rather than the alternative: kept the engine's `DesignPipelineInput.noFreshen` / `noFill` contract exactly as-is (design-pipeline/index.ts:55 and :90 still skip a phase only on `=== true`) and corrected only the command layer's option read. The defect is at the command boundary; the engine contract is coherent and is consumed by tests and callers beyond this command.

Used `opts.freshen === false` / `opts.fill === false` rather than a truthiness check (`!opts.freshen`). Empirically verified against the exact commander in use (12.1.0): Commander ALWAYS populates `freshen`/`fill`, defaulting both to `true`, so only an explicit `false` distinguishes 'flag passed' from 'flag absent'. A `=== undefined` test would never fire. This also preserves the command's established contract of OMITTING unsupplied flags from the input rather than sending `false` for them.

Also corrected the `DesignPipelineCliOptions` interface (`noFreshen?`/`noFill?` -> `freshen`/`fill`). This is part of the same root cause, not scope creep: the interface asserted a shape Commander never produces, which is precisely why the inert reads typechecked cleanly and the bug survived review. Leaving it would let the same defect be reintroduced silently. Review round 2 additionally dropped the `?` from both fields (design-pipeline.ts:41-42): the JSDoc directly above already stated Commander populates them on every parse, so declaring them optional contradicted the file's own documented invariant and left an `=== undefined` read looking legitimate. Safe because the interface is local to design-pipeline.ts and is used only as the `.action()` parameter type — there is no object-literal construction of it anywhere in the repo.

INVERTED AN EXISTING PASSING TEST. At the pre-fix revision (c7bdb08c6~1), packages/cli/tests/commands/design-pipeline-command.test.ts:140-172 was a deliberate CHARACTERIZATION block that pinned the BROKEN behavior (asserting the input does NOT contain `noFreshen`/`noFill`). Those three assertions now assert the opposite. This is intended: the original block's own comment stated 'These tests will go red the moment it lands, which is exactly the signal wanted.' A reviewer must see that a previously-passing assertion changed meaning. The replacement block is at :139-205 in the current tree.

Added guard tests beyond a straight inversion, covering the over-correction: a bare run must still OMIT both keys, and each flag alone must not set the other's key. Without these, a fix keyed off key-presence rather than `=== false` would pass the inverted assertions while skipping every phase on every run. The guards pass in the pre-fix and post-fix states by design; they constrain the fix, they do not reproduce the bug. Review round 2 added the missing MIRROR half (design-pipeline-command.test.ts:201-204, '--no-fill alone must not set noFreshen'): round 1 shipped only the `--no-freshen` direction, and a mutation probe confirmed the asymmetry was load-bearing — mutating the `fill` branch to also set `input.noFreshen` survived the round-1 suite (47 passed) and fails the round-2 suite.

Held scope to design-pipeline.ts only. Two sibling instances of the identical defect class were found in the same sweep and deliberately NOT touched: test-craft.ts:86 (`opts.noSourcePair === true` against `.option('--no-source-pair')` at :40, tracked as issue #1882, separate lane in flight) and dashboard.ts:121 (`opts.noOpen !== true` against `.option('--no-open')` at :132, tracked as issue #1956).

CORRECTION (review round 2) — a claim in this file's round-1 revision was FALSE and is withdrawn. It named `fleet/budget-check.ts:170` as a third broken sibling and added that ':219 already uses the correct form in the same file as its broken :170 read'. There is no broken read in budget-check.ts. Line 219 is line 170's PRODUCER, not a second site: the `.action()` at :211-221 normalizes `noRefresh: opts.refresh === false` (carrying the comment 'Commander maps --no-refresh to refresh: false; normalize to noRefresh') and hands the normalized object to the separately-exported `runBudgetCheck()` at :165, whose `if (!opts.noRefresh)` at :170 consumes it. `runBudgetCheck` is also called directly from unit tests with an explicit `noRefresh: true`, so 'fixing' :170 to read a positive `refresh` key would have broken them. Acting on the withdrawn claim would have introduced a defect, not removed one. The repo-wide enumeration that settles this — all 13 `.option('--no-...')` declarations, every one under packages/cli/src/commands/ — is tabulated at issue #1956 and is cited here rather than re-derived. Nine of the thirteen are correct (install.ts:459, adoption.ts:370, distortion.ts:155, mcp.ts:243, fix-drift.ts:48, recommend.ts:138, predict.ts:177, agent/review.ts:179, budget-check.ts:219); the four broken ones are this PR's two plus test-craft.ts:86 and dashboard.ts:121.

Three review findings adjacent to this fix were filed as follow-ups rather than grown into this PR, which is scoped `Closes #1881`. Two of them are reachable only BECAUSE this fix works — the flags previously could not skip anything, so no skipped-phase output state existed. #1958: with FRESHEN genuinely skipped, printPipelineResult (design-pipeline.ts:110-154, render at :119-125) prints `newContext()`'s untouched `false` defaults as measurements, reporting `DESIGN.md=no tokens.json=no` for a project where the files exist, and `--json` serializes the same values with no skip marker. #1960: with FILL genuinely skipped, `anyBootstrap` (report.ts:46) stays false and computeVerdict (report.ts:56-64) returns `pass` for a design-system-less project that reports `warn` without the flag — a false-green verdict, though not an exit-code regression since both map to 0. #1959: `--ci` is a separate, pre-existing inert flag on this same command (declared design-pipeline.ts:59, written :78, accepted at design-pipeline/index.ts:35, read by nothing; `FixInput` at phases/fix.ts:21-26 has no `ci` field), and the green test at design-pipeline-command.test.ts:104-107 reads as coverage while proving only that a value reaches a field with no readers.
rootCause: Commander's negated-flag convention applied backwards. `.option('--no-freshen')` defines an option named `freshen` (default `true`, set to `false` when passed) and never produces a `noFreshen` key. The action read `opts.noFreshen === true` / `opts.noFill === true`, which are `undefined` on every code path, so `input.noFreshen` / `input.noFill` were never set and the engine always ran FRESHEN and FILL. Two documented flags were silently inert, failing in the worst direction: FILL is the expensive phase the flag exists to avoid.
